texts.preamble: Ravi Shankar Narayan Singh vs Rashi Sehgal on 19 January, 2016 In The Court Of Ms. Geetanjli Goel, Po: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal2, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Suit No.D256/15 Date of Institution: 30.07.2015
texts.facts: Vide this judgmentcumaward, I proceed to decide the DAR which is treated as claim petition u/s 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, as amended uptodate (hereinafter referred to as the Act) for grant of compensation in a road accident. 2. It is the case of the petitioner that on 13.02.2015 he was waiting for bus for going to Dwarka. In the meantime, suddenly the offending vehicle bearing No.HR51AQ6056 which was coming from Ravi Shankar Narayan Singh vs Rashi Sehgal on 19 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178386289/ 1 the wrong side hit the petitioner. Due to the forceful impact, the petitioner fell down on the road. It is contended that the offending vehicle was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, rashly, negligently and due to the sudden forceful impact the petitioner was injured and sustained grievous injuries. It is stated that in respect of the accident, FIR No.57/15 under sections 279/388 IPC was registered at PS Delhi Cantt. 3. It is submitted that the petitioner was taken to Bhagat Chandra Hospital, Palam for giving first aid treatment where the concerned doctors prepared the MLC of the injured. After that the injured was removed to Base Hospital, Delhi Cantt. where the injured was admitted three times from 13.02.2015 to 11.03.2015, 22.04.2015 to 06.06.2015 and again from 18.07.2015 to 14.08.2015. It is averred that the petitioner, at the time of the accident was working in Indian Army as Nayak and was drawing a monthly salary of Rs. Suit No. D256/15 Ravi Shankar v Rashi Sehgal & Ors. 27,000/ per month. It is contended that the petitioner would have made and established a big estate from his savings and income in due course, thus the estate of the petitioner had suffered a big setback due to the accident. It is averred that the petitioner had become medically unfit for his promotion and for serving in active operational areas. Army Medical authorities had put several restrictions on the employment of the petitioner for various Army duties. Therefore, the petitioner lost the privilege and sense of professional achievement to attain the prestigious appointments. It is submitted that the petitioner was claiming compensation on account of loss of income, loss of estate, loss of future prospects and loss of expectancy of life and other general and special damages according to the law. It is stated that the petitioner was bed ridden for about 7 months due to the accident and he had spent a sum of Rs.35,000/ on the medical treatment. The doctor had advised the petitioner to take complete bed rest and to take special/ rich protein diet and he had spent a sum of Rs.25,000/ on special diet and he had also spent sum of Rs.20,000/ on conveyance. It is averred that at the time of the accident the petitioner was 25 years of age possessing good health and sound mind and robust physic. Due to the accident he and his family members had suffered great mental stress, harassment and agony besides financial losses. It is contended that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.HR 51AQ6056. Suit No. D256/15 Ravi Shankar v Rashi Sehgal & Ors. 4. Reply was filed on behalf of respondent No.1 to the DAR stating therein that as per the statement of the injured, he could not identify the lady who was driving the vehicle at the time of the alleged accident. Even as per the Investigating Officer he could not find any eye witness to the accident at the place of accident. It is contended that the IO during investigation enquired from Faridabad Ravi Shankar Narayan Singh vs Rashi Sehgal on 19 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178386289/ 2 Transport Authority regarding the ownership of the alleged car bearing registration No.HR51AQ 6056 and found that the car was registered in the name of Rashi Gaba daughter of Kaushal Gaba resident of 526, Sector37, Faridabad, Haryana. The Investigating Officer also served the owner of the car with notice under Section 133 M. V. Act who according to the IO had allegedly stated that she was the registered owner of the car and on 13.02.2015 at about 8.30 a.m. she was driving the car. Except the said statement which was recorded by the IO without the knowledge and consent of the respondent No.1, there was no other eye witness or any other evidence to connect the owner of the vehicle Rashi with the commission of the accident, resulting in injuries to the injured on account of driving rashly and negligently the car which struck against the injured. It is submitted that the said car was never driven by the owner at the time and place of accident and she had been falsely implicated. It is averred that there is no evidence connecting the owner of the vehicle with the commission of the accident dated 13.02.2015 at about 8.30 a.m. and the said vehicle was comprehensively insured vide insurance policy No.922543211010148 which was insured with Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. on 13.03.2014 and the said insurance was valid from Suit No. D256/15 Ravi Shankar v Rashi Sehgal & Ors. Page no. 4 of 26 13.03.2014 to 12.03.2015. It is alleged that even in the mechanical inspection report no fresh damages were found on the car as per the inspection report of the Mechanical Inspection Officer dated 08.03.2015. 5. Reply was filed on behalf of the respondent No.2 stating therein that the Accidents Information Report as framed was vague and lacked material particulars. It is submitted that the alleged accident, if any had taken place solely due to the negligence of the injured, who himself was careless about his own safety. The alleged driver of the insured vehicle (Chevrolet Beat) bearing registration No.HR51AQ6056 had nothing to do with the alleged accident, as the injured himself was the author of the unfortunate accident. It is averred that assuming but not admitting the involvement of the insured vehicle (Chevrolet Beat) bearing registration No.HR51AQ6056 as true, in that event, the injured was careless about his own safety. Legal offer of Rs.35,000/ excluding the amount of actual medical bills was made. 6. Vide order dated 21.09.2015 from the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed: 1. The petitioner Shri Ravi Shankar Narayan Singh himself appeared in the witness box as PW1 and led his evidence by way of affidavit which is Ex.PW1/A. The petitioner was also examined on 12.10.2015 in terms of the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court on 11.1.2013 in MACA No.792/2006 titled Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Ranjit Pandey and Ors. 9. The case of the petitioner is that on 13.02.2015 he was waiting for bus for going to Dwarka. In the meantime, suddenly the offending vehicle bearing No.HR51AQ6056 which was coming from the wrong side hit the petitioner. It was contended that the offending vehicle was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, rashly, negligently and due to the sudden forceful impact the petitioner was injured and sustained grievous injuries. It was stated that in respect of the accident, FIR No.57/15 under sections 279/388 IPC was registered at PS Delhi Cantt. The petitioner had also deposed to that effect. 12. The IO had filed Detailed Accident Report containing the criminal record consisting of copy of charge sheet; copy of tehrir, copy of FIR; copy of site plan; copy of MLC, copy of seizure memos; copy of DD, copy of mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, copy of verification report of the RC of the offending vehicle with the copy of RC, copy of DL of the respondent No. 1 with its verification report, copy of the insurance policy of the offending vehicle and its verification report, copy of arrest memo and personal search memo, copy of order on application for release of the offending vehicle on superdari along with a copy of the indemnity bond and copies of photographs. As per the FIR No.57/15 under sections 279/337 IPC, PS Delhi Cantt the case was registered on the basis of complaint of SI Kaptan Singh (on DD). As per the charge sheet the respondent No.1 has been charge sheeted for the offence under sections 279/338 IPC. Suit No. D256/15 Ravi Shankar v Rashi Sehgal & Ors. 13. The respondent No.1 who is the owner and driver of the alleged offending vehicle had filed the reply averring that as per the statement of the injured, he could not identify the lady who was Ravi Shankar Narayan Singh vs Rashi Sehgal on 19 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178386289/ 5 driving the vehicle at the time of the alleged accident. It was contended that the IO during investigation enquired from Faridabad Transport Authority regarding the ownership of the alleged car bearing registration No.HR51AQ6056 and found that the car was registered in the name of Rashi Gaba daughter of Kaushal Gaba resident of 526, Sector37, Faridabad, Haryana. After that the injured was removed to Base Suit No. D256/15 Ravi Shankar v Rashi Sehgal & Ors. Page no. 16 of 26 Hospital, Delhi Cantt. where the injured was admitted three times from 13.02.2015 to 11.03.2015, 22.04.2015 to 06.06.2015 and again from 18.07.2015 to 14.08.2015. Thus PW1 stated that he resumed his Suit No. D256/15 Ravi Shankar v Rashi Sehgal & Ors. Page no. 20 of 26 services on 24.08.2015 after the accident. Thus PW1 stated that Suit No. D256/15 Ravi Shankar v Rashi Sehgal & Ors. he resumed his services on 24.08.2015 after the accident i.e. after more than 6 months of the accident. He had volunteered that he did not receive salary for the treatment period and that he had taken 12 weeks sick leave. The respondent No.1 is the driver cum owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Thus the respondents No.1 and 2 are held jointly and severally liable.
texts.arguments: It is submitted that the insurance company would not be liable on account of breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy if the driver of the vehicle bearing registration No.HR51AQ6056 was found not having any valid and effective driving license for the particular category of vehicle, which he was found to be driving at the time of the alleged accident. It is averred that the policy cum certificate No. 9202542311010148 was issued in favour of Ms. Rashi Gaba, the registered owner of the vehicle at the time of issuance of the Insurance Policy valid from 13.03.2014 to 12.03.2015. It is contended that there was contributory negligence on the part of the injured and the alleged accident took place Suit No. D256/15 Ravi Shankar v Rashi Sehgal & Ors. Page no. 5 of 26 entirely due to the negligence on the part of the injured, who was careless about his own safety. To determine the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle it has been held in National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Pushpa Rana & Another 2009 Accident Claims Journal 287 as follows: "The last contention of the appellant insurance company is that the respondents/claimants should have proved negligence on the part of the driver and in this regard the counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. V. Meena Variyal (supra). On perusal Suit No. D256/15 Ravi Shankar v Rashi Sehgal & Ors. Page no. 7 of 26 of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced: (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in FIR No.955 of 2004, pertaining to involvement of offending vehicle (ii) criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of charge sheet under sections 279/304A, Indian Penal Code against the driver; (iii) certified copy of FIR, wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of deceased. These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent. Proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict Ravi Shankar Narayan Singh vs Rashi Sehgal on 19 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178386289/ 4 rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard. Hence, this contention of the counsel for the appellant also falls face down. There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on part of the driver." In Kaushnamma Begum and others v. New India Assurance Company Limited, it was inter alia held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the issue of wrongful act or omission on the part of the driver of the motor vehicle involved in the accident has been left to a secondary importance and mere use or involvement of motor vehicle in causing bodily injury or death to a human being or damage to property would make the petition maintainable under Sections 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act. Suit No. D256/15 Ravi Shankar v Rashi Sehgal & Ors. 11. In Basant Kaur and others v. Chattar Pal Singh and others 2003 ACJ 369 MP (DB) it was observed that registration of criminal case against the driver of the offending vehicle was enough to record a finding that the driver of the offending vehicle was responsible for causing the accident. Suit No. D256/15 Ravi Shankar v Rashi Sehgal & Ors. It was submitted that the petitioner was claiming compensation on account of loss of income, loss of estate, loss of future prospects and loss of expectancy of life and other general and special damages according to the law. It was stated that the petitioner was bed ridden for about 7 months due to the accident and he had spent a sum of Rs.35,000/ on the medical treatment. The doctor had advised the petitioner to take complete bed rest. It was averred that at the time of the accident the petitioner was 25 years of age possessing good health and sound mind and robust physic. Due to the accident he and his family members had suffered great mental stress, harassment and agony besides financial losses. The petitioner had also deposed to that effect. Page no. 15 of 26 petitioner had filed bill for an amount of Rs.500/. Looking to the nature of the injuries the petitioner is held entitled to the amount of the bill. The petitioner would have incurred some expenses even subsequently. Accordingly an amount of Rs.2,000/ is awarded towards medical treatment and expenses including the amount of the bill. It has been held in Divisional Controller, K. S. R. T. C v Mahadeva Shetty and another AIR 2003 Supreme Court 4172 as under: 13."The damages for vehicular accidents are in the nature of compensation in money for loss of any kind caused to any person. In the later case there is possibility of repair or restoration. In Parry V. Cleaver (1969 1 All. E. R. 555) Lord Morris stated as follows: Ravi Shankar Narayan Singh vs Rashi Sehgal on 19 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178386289/ 8 "To compensate in money for pain and for the physical consequences is invariably difficult, but...... no other process can be devised than that of making monetary assessment." The case of the petitioner is that due to the sudden forceful impact of the accident on 13.2.2015, the petitioner was injured and sustained grievous injuries. It was stated that the petitioner was bed ridden for about 7 months due to the accident. The MLC of the petitioner is on record which shows the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the nature of injuries was opined to be grievous. The documents placed on record show that the petitioner had sustained minor head injury and liver laceration Grade III Haemothorax right. The documents also show that he remained admitted in hospital from time to time. However there is nothing to show that the petitioner had sustained any disability in the accident. Looking at the nature of injuries and extent of treatment and that the accident pertains to the year 2015, the petitioner is awarded Rs.30,000/ (Rs.Thirty Thousand only) for pain and suffering. As such he would have been more than 24 years old on the date of the accident i.e. 13.2.2015. 23. The petitioner in para 11 of his affidavit Ex.PW1/A had deposed that the doctor had advised him to take special/ rich protein diet and he had spent a sum of Rs.25,000/ on special diet. During crossexamination by the learned counsel for the insurance company PW1 stated that he had not placed on record any document to show that he was advised special diet. Although the petitioner has not proved that he was advised special diet but looking at the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner notice can be taken of the fact that the petitioner might have taken diet rich in protein, vitamins and minerals for speedier recovery. In the circumstances the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/ (Rs.Five Thousand only) for special diet. 24. Although the petitioner has not produced any evidence to show that he incurred any expenses towards attendant charges, however looking to the nature of injuries the petitioner would have incurred some expenditure on attendant charges and a sum of Rs.15,000/ is awarded towards attendant charges. LOSS OF INCOME 25. It is the case of the petitioner that at the time of the accident he was working in Indian Army as Nayak and was drawing a monthly salary of Rs. 27,000/ per month. It was contended that the petitioner would have made and established a big estate from his savings and income in due course, thus the Suit No. D256/15 Ravi Shankar v Rashi Sehgal & Ors. Page no. 19 of 26 estate of the petitioner had suffered a big setback due to the accident. It was averred that the petitioner had become medically unfit for his promotion and for serving in active operational areas. Army Medical authorities had put several restrictions on the employment of the petitioner for various Army duties. Therefore, the petitioner lost the privilege and sense of professional achievement to attain the prestigious appointments. Accordingly the petitioner cannot be Ravi Shankar Narayan Singh vs Rashi Sehgal on 19 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178386289/ 11 held entitled to any amount on account of loss of future prospects.
